messages:
anya: quick flag: ruby sampleapp streamed sessions in staging threw a bunch of 401s during an automated token rotation test. Looks like the persistent connection kept the old Authorization header for ~2s.

ryan: is this using the new refresh helper or the legacy refresh callback?

anya: new helper (TokenRefresher) wired into client.init. repro: start a long stream, replace token file mid-stream.

pat: can you paste the tiny repro snippet?

anya: sure:
```ruby
client = Redwood::Client.new(token: File.read('/tmp/token'))
client.stream('chat.completions') do |m|
  puts m
end
# then overwrite /tmp/token after 1s to simulate rotation
```
Observed: stream receives repeated 401 responses until the client reconnects ~2s later.

ryan: probable cause: header cached on the Net::HTTP persistent connection. We fixed similar in other SDKs by rebuilding the connection on auth failures.

pat: proposed patch: on stream 401, call TokenRefresher.refresh and force recreate_connection. Add a guard so transient 429s don't trigger rebuild.

anya: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/438 (branch: anya/stream-reconnect-on-401). Tests pass locally.

ci-bot: CI results: ruby-3.1 PASS, jruby-9.3 PASS, macos-arm flaky (rerun queued).

ryan: assigning review to @pat. If low risk, backport to v1.x as a patch and add changelog and a quickstart note about token rotation during long streams. Also add a tiny integration test in sampleapp that rotates token mid-stream so we catch regressions.

pat: will review today. Thanks for the repro, that made triage much faster. :thumbsup:
